defects.description: Step 4 builds its own readline y/N prompt and non-TTY refusal inside rollback.ts instead of reusing confirm() from src/ui/prompt.ts, which deploy uses and which already implements --yes skipping, the non-interactive refusal, and the y/yes answer check.
Step 4 refuses a non-interactive session without --yes by throwing AbortError, whose exitCode is 1 (src/errors.ts). R3/AC1 require this case to be a usage error with exit code 2 (UsageError).
defects.location: plan.md step 4; fixture/src/errors.ts; spec.md R3, AC1

defects.description: Step 7 prints human progress lines with console.log and hand-rolled ANSI colours, bypassing the shared Output class (src/ui/output.ts) that all commands write through. This ignores Output's injected stdout (so tests using capture() cannot see the lines) and duplicates its TTY colour handling.

Step 8 emits the NDJSON state and result events through Output.result(), but Output.result() in --json mode writes JSON.stringify(data, null, 2), i.e. indented multi-line JSON. Each event therefore spans several lines, so stdout is not NDJSON and AC3 ('every stdout line parses as JSON on its own') fails.
defects.location: plan.md step 8; fixture/src/ui/output.ts; spec.md R6, AC3

defects.description: Step 6 polls GET /rollbacks/:id every 1 s (POLL_MS = 1_000), i.e. 60 requests/minute: the entire per-token limit from the spec's non-functional constraints, which is shared with other commands such as a concurrent deploy --wait (another 12/min at deploy's 5 s POLL_MS). ApiClient does not retry 429 (only 502/503/504), so a throttled poll throws ApiError and the wait fails with exit 1; AC6 is not met.
defects.location: plan.md step 6; spec.md non-functional constraints, AC6; fixture/src/api/client.ts; fixture/src/commands/deploy.ts

defects.description: Step 9 signals a wait timeout by throwing AbortError, whose exitCode is 1 (src/errors.ts); R5/AC2 require exit code 3 for a timeout.
defects.location: plan.md step 9; fixture/src/errors.ts; spec.md R5, AC2

defects.description: Test strategy has no automated test for AC1 (non-TTY without --yes exits 2 with no POST), defers AC2 (timeout exit 3) to a manual staging game day although sleep is injectable and a clock could be too, and has nothing for AC6 (poll rate). The --json --wait test only checks that state events exist and the last event, not that each line parses alone or that there is one state line per transition.
Step 2 defaults --timeout to 15m, but R1 specifies a default of 10m.

tensions.description: Architecture sees the inline prompt duplicating confirm() and recommends swapping it in; confirm() refuses non-TTY sessions with AbortError, exactly as the plan describes, so the swap looks behaviour-preserving. Consistency sees that AbortError exits 1 (errors.ts) while R3/AC1 require exit 2, and recommends throwing UsageError in the refusal path. Combined, they conflict: once the shared confirm() is used, the refusal is confirm()'s AbortError and exits 1 again. Changing confirm() to throw UsageError would change deploy's behaviour (out of scope) and break deploy.test.ts, which asserts AbortError.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Replace the inline readline prompt in rollback.ts with confirm() from src/ui/prompt.ts.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Throw UsageError (exit 2) instead of AbortError when the session is non-interactive and --yes is absent.
tensions.reconciliation: In rollback.ts, check !isTTY && !yes first and throw UsageError (exit 2) before any API write; then call the shared confirm() for the interactive path (which still exits 1 on a declined prompt). Leave prompt.ts, AbortError, and deploy's exit-1 behaviour unchanged, and add a test that the non-TTY path exits 2 with zero POST calls.

tensions.description: Architecture wants every line of rollback output to go through Output instead of console.log. Consistency sees that the Output.result() route the plan uses for NDJSON pretty-prints (JSON.stringify with indent 2), so events span multiple lines, and recommends writing each event as a compact single-line JSON.stringify to stdout, or making Output.result() compact. Writing to stdout directly reintroduces the bypass architecture objected to; making result() compact changes deploy's --json output, which is out of scope. Routing everything through today's Output cannot produce NDJSON.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Remove console.log and ANSI codes from rollback.ts and send all output through Output (line/ok/result).
tensions.lens_b_fix: Emit each state/result event as a single-line JSON.stringify(event) on stdout (or change Output.result to compact JSON) so each line parses on its own.
tensions.reconciliation: Add a new event(data, humanText) method to Output that writes compact single-line JSON in --json mode and a TTY-aware human line otherwise. Use it for every state change and for the final {event: 'result'} line under --wait; keep result() (indented) for the no-wait single object and for deploy, so deploy's output and tests are unchanged. Test that each stdout line parses alone.
